text: Knockdown of LGALS3BP (depleted from APOE4 lysosomes) in HsAPOE3 Neuro-2a cells reduced LysoTracker staining, modestly alkalinized lysosomal pH and nearly halved lysosomal density, implicating LGALS3BP loss as a partial driver of the APOE4 alkalinization phenotype (reported: LysoTracker ~0.72x of siScr; lysosomal density ~0.55x; pH change described as modest).
description: HsAPOE3 Neuro-2a cells transfected with Lgals3bp siRNA vs scrambled control for 48 h; LysoTracker, OregonGreen-dextran ratiometric pH and density quantification, Magic Red cathepsin B; three independent experiments. Also validated in human WTC11 CRISPRi iPSC-derived neurons where LGALS3BP knockdown decreased LysoTracker staining (Fig 4H-I). Caveat: knockdown is a surrogate for APOE4; mouse cell line plus human iNeu.

provenance.excerpt: We found that LGALS3BP depletion markedly decreased the LysoTracker staining in healthy HsAPOE3 Neuro-2a cells (Figure 4A,B). To assess whether this was driven by changes in lysosomal acidification or the density of lysosomes, we loaded the Neuro-2a cells with Dextran-Oregon Green, finding that LGALS3BP knockdown modestly alkalinized the lysosomal pH, but nearly halved the lysosomal density (Figure 4C-E).
